newsitem.title: UK: Eramet concerned at copper price dominance on LME.
newsitem.headline: Eramet concerned at copper price dominance on LME.

text.p: French nickel producer Eramet is concerned about the amount of influence the London Metal Exchange's (LME) flagship copper contract has on prices for other industrial metals.

"It is clear that the evolution of the copper price has an influence on the nickel price for some reason," Eramet chairman Yves Rambaud said after a presentation to the Association of Mining Analysts on Thursday.
"Yes we are concerned (about the LME nickel market)," Rambaud said. "It is becoming more and more difficult for producers to understand why the level of the nickel price is where it is," he added.
Consumers were also vulnerable to nickel price volatility caused by movements in the copper market, he said.
"We take this as a signal to consumers not to rely too much on the LME," he said.
He said Eramet does not hedge its annual production of around 53,000 tonnes of nickel on the LME. But the group's nickel selling price was closely linked with LME values.
Eramet does not use fixed price contracts in any major way, but would be prepared to dicuss the possibility with its customers, he said.

"But with prices at around $3.50 per pound ($7,716/tonne), they (consumers) don't care about the volatility of the price too much," he said. Rambaud said that Eramet has not approached the LME formally to express its concern over nickel price volatility.
Along with other base metals, nickel values fell sharply in the wake of Sumitomo Corp's announcement in June that it had run up huge losses in unauthorised copper dealings.
On Thursday the company upgraded its estimate of the losses to $2.6 billion from $1.8 billion earlier.
Benchmark three month nickel futures fell to a 15-month low of $6,910 a tonne in August, partly as a result of heavy falls in the price of copper.
Values have since recovered to around $7,400.
